set_aside.subject: K-05 admission verdict when the trial corpus changes
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus” does not say what happens to a recorded verdict or its activation when a case is later added to that contract version’s corpus.
set_aside.question: When the active corpus changes, does an earlier admitted verdict cease to qualify immediately, and if so what happens to the implementation’s existing activation and how can that implementation obtain a verdict over the new corpus?
options: The earlier verdict remains historical but the activation remains usable until another implementation is submitted.
The earlier verdict no longer qualifies and the existing activation is removed or made unusable immediately.
The earlier implementation is automatically evaluated against the enlarged corpus and receives a new recorded verdict.
Resubmitting the same implementation explicitly evaluates it against the enlarged corpus.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the verdict as applying to an exact corpus revision, keep it as history, invalidate the activation when that revision is no longer current, and allow explicit resubmission to evaluate the existing implementation against the new corpus.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active for contract version C after passing its only trial case A.
events: An author adds case B to C’s corpus.
B fails when I is executed.
An owner or agent starts a flow whose function node uses C.
outcomes: The run starts and uses I because its existing activation remains current despite the enlarged corpus.
The start is refused because I has no admitted verdict over C’s current corpus and its activation is no longer usable.
witness.observer: The owner or agent starting the flow

set_aside.subject: K-05 production of a recorded admission verdict
set_aside.text: Replacing “a deterministic verdict” with “one recorded verdict” leaves unspecified which executions or existing evidence determine that verdict when an implementation can behave nondeterministically through an undetected source of time or chance allowed by K-02.
set_aside.question: For one admission attempt, how many times is each active case executed, may prior trial evidence be reused, and how are differing results for the same case combined into the single recorded verdict?
options: Execute each active case once and aggregate those fresh results.
Reuse the latest recorded trial evidence for each case.
Execute cases a fixed number of times and refuse if any execution fails.
Repeat until a pass or failure condition is met.
set_aside.default_guess: Execute every active case exactly once afresh for the admission attempt and refuse if any of those executions fails.

witness.initial: Contract C has one case whose expected result is produced only when implementation I obtains one of two values from an undetected source of chance.
events: An author submits I for admission.
The kernel evaluates the active corpus.
outcomes: The kernel executes the case once, observes the expected result, and records admitted.
The kernel executes the case more than once, observes at least one mismatch, and records refused.
witness.observer: The author and anyone inspecting or attempting to use C’s activation

set_aside.subject: K-05 repeated submission of an implementation with a recorded verdict
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict” does not say whether submitting the same immutable implementation again returns its existing verdict, performs another admission and appends a verdict, or replaces the recorded verdict.
set_aside.question: What must happen when equal implementation content is submitted again while the contract version’s corpus is unchanged?
options: Return the existing recorded verdict without executing the corpus again.
Run admission again and retain every verdict.
Run admission again and replace the earlier verdict.
Refuse another admission because one verdict already exists.
set_aside.default_guess: Return the existing verdict while the implementation and corpus revision are unchanged.

witness.initial: Implementation I was refused after a nondeterministic execution failed case A; neither I nor the corpus has changed.
events: The author submits byte-identical code for I again.
A fresh execution of A would pass.
outcomes: The kernel returns the recorded refusal and I remains inactive.
The kernel evaluates I again, records admission, and activates it.
witness.observer: The author and callers of flows using the contract version
